title: Working Out the Points a Statement-Credit Redemption Uses on Personal Credit Cards
content:
### The settlement target

The settlement target is the fees and the interest posted to the card account in the last month, less the fee reversals credited to it in the last month, and never less than 0.00 USD.

### The covered share and the redemption value

The covered share is 55 percent. The redemption value is the tier's own cash value per point.

### From the target to a point count

The settlement target multiplied by the covered share is divided by the redemption value and the quotient is rounded half-up to a whole point. The redemption uses the lesser of that point count and the unredeemed points standing on the card account.

### Where nothing is redeemed

Where the point count so obtained is below the tier's own redemption minimum, no statement-credit redemption is made and nothing is posted.

### Worked on hypothetical figures

A card under Personal Credit Cards carries 260.00 USD of fees and interest posted in the last month and 20.00 USD of fee reversals credited in the same month, so the settlement target is 240.00 USD. Multiplied by 55 percent that is 132.00 USD. On a tier whose cash value is 0.01 USD a point, the quotient is 13200 points, already whole. Where 15000 unredeemed points stand on the account, the redemption uses 13200 points; where only 9000 stand, it uses 9000.

A second card carries 18.00 USD of fees and interest in the last month and no fee reversal, giving a settlement target of 18.00 USD and a covered amount of 9.90 USD, which at 0.01 USD a point is 990 points. On a tier whose redemption minimum is 2500 points, 990 is below it and nothing is posted.

A third card carries 4.00 USD of fees and interest and 11.00 USD of fee reversals in the last month. The difference is below zero, so the settlement target is 0.00 USD and the covered amount is 0.00 USD.
